hook.line: Sooner or later a friend asks, "Should I do it?" A flat yes feels cold. Telling them they are right (or wrong) to do it gives your opinion and shows you are on their side.
hook.es: Haces bien en no firmar nada hoy.
hook.en: You're right not to sign anything today.

rule:
To say someone is right to do something, use *haces bien en* plus an infinitive. To say they are wrong, use *haces mal en*.

The verb is *hacer* (to do), so it changes with the person: *haces* (you), *hace* (he or she), *hacemos* (we), *hacen* (they). For the past, *hiciste bien en* means "you were right to".

Always *en*, never *de* or *a*. To say someone is right *not* to do it, put *no* before the infinitive: *Haces bien en no firmar nada.*

English says "you are right". Spanish says "you do well".
smallPrint: Teachers call this a verb phrase: *hacer* plus *bien* or *mal*, then *en* and an infinitive. English has a close cousin in "you do well to wait".

yourTurn.prompt: You're right to wait for Vale (to a friend). Pick *bien* or *mal* and type the whole sentence: *Haces ___ en esperar a Vale.*
yourTurn.answer: Haces bien en esperar a Vale.
yourTurn.why: *Bien* says the person is right to do it.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: You're wrong to argue with Hernando. (to a friend)
yourTurn.answer: Haces mal en discutir con Hernando.
yourTurn.why: *Mal* says they are wrong, and *en* comes before the infinitive.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: They're right to close early.
Type in Spanish: He's right not to sell the café.
yourTurn.answer: Hace bien en no vender el café.
accept: Él hace bien en no vender el café.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it about *we*: *Haces bien en esperar a Vale.* Say: We're right to wait for Vale.
yourTurn.answer: Hacemos bien en esperar a Vale.
yourTurn.why: Only *hacer* changes with the person; the infinitive stays the same.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it "right not to": *Haces bien en llamar a Mariana.* Say: You're right not to call Mariana. (to a friend)
yourTurn.answer: Haces bien en no llamar a Mariana.
yourTurn.why: Put *no* in front of the infinitive.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: You were right to tell the truth. (to a friend)
yourTurn.answer: Hiciste bien en decir la verdad.
yourTurn.why: *Hiciste* is the past of *haces*: "you did well".

pitfalls.wrong: Haces bien de esperar a Vale.
pitfalls.right: Haces bien en esperar a Vale.
pitfalls.why: Almost. With *haces bien* the link word is *en*, not *de*.

pitfalls.wrong: Eres bien en esperar a Vale.
pitfalls.right: Haces bien en esperar a Vale.
pitfalls.why: Almost. English says "you are right", but Spanish says "you do well", so the verb is *hacer*.

pitfalls.wrong: Haces bien en esperando a Vale.
pitfalls.right: Haces bien en esperar a Vale.
pitfalls.why: Almost. After *en* use the plain infinitive, not an *-ing* form.

pitfalls.wrong: Haces bien no esperar a Vale.
pitfalls.right: Haces bien en no esperar a Vale.

personal: Tell a friend about something they did well or badly, starting with *Hiciste bien en* or *Haces mal en*.
